findings.message: The unquoted `$@` splits file operands on whitespace and expands glob characters before `lk_check_files` receives them. A readable path such as `my file.txt` can be treated as multiple operands, and a literal glob path can expand unexpectedly. Quote it as `"$@"`.
Invalid `-n` values are usage errors under the documented convention, but this branch prints no usage line and exits 1. Use `lk_usage_error` so it prints the usage line and exits 2.

parsed.summary: Both findings are confirmed: file operands are expanded unsafely, and invalid `-n` values do not follow the documented usage-error behavior.

pull_request.title: number: add -n START to begin numbering at START
pull_request.body:
Adds `-n START` to `linekit number`, so a numbered excerpt can keep the line numbers of the file it was cut from:

    sed -n 120,140p f | linekit number -n 120

The command table in README.md is updated.
